pk.context: 400 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: very dark yellow to brownish orange, film-coated, ovaloid, scored tablet

tell: The Philadelphia chromosome target, BCR-ABL, identifies the CML kinase inhibitor imatinib.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is 98%, with about 95% bound to plasma proteins, mostly albumin. Elimination is mainly fecal, about 68% of a dose within 7 days, largely as metabolites.
A mesylate salt of molecular weight 589.7, against 493.6 for the free base. Soluble in acidic aqueous buffers but very slightly soluble to insoluble at neutral or alkaline pH.
Film-coated tablets of 100 and 400 mg, marketed under an NDA and dosed once daily.
No boxed warning and no contraindications. Edema, often periorbital, and nausea with vomiting are the most frequently reported drug-related reactions.
Philadelphia chromosome positive chronic myeloid and acute lymphoblastic leukemias, and myelodysplastic or myeloproliferative diseases with PDGFR gene re-arrangements.
Inhibits the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase created by the Philadelphia chromosome, and also the receptor kinases for PDGF and stem cell factor (c-Kit).
The generic name begins with I and has eight letters.
